newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal parliament puts finance minister on spot.
newsitem.headline: Portugal parliament puts finance minister on spot.

text.p: Portugal's parliament launched on Wednesday a formal probe into a financial guarantee given by Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco to a trades union linked to the ruling Socialist government.

The minister's decision to guarantee a 600 million escudos ($3.4 million) loan to the moderate General Workers Union (UGT), traditionally close to the Socialists, provoked a political storm with opposition parties branding the move as illegal.
Parliament, where the government is four seats short of a majority, voted to set up a special commission to probe the guarantee. The Socialists abstained in the vote.

"(This commission) must analyse both the legality of the whole process and...the political circumstances in which the minister took the decision," said opposition Social Democrat member Marques Guedes.
"For our part, (the guarantee) is illegal and unjust," he added.

Opposition parties suspect that the loan, granted by the state savings bank Caixa de Geral de Depositos, was offered to the union as an inducement to sign earlier this year an accord limiting wage rises in the public sector.

Sousa Franco, a former head of the Court of Accounts, the state's auditor, has reacted angrily to accusations of wrongdoing, warning that he will suspend the granting of all types of government guarantees until the probe has been concluded.

The minister is not a member of the Socialist Party. He was drafted into the government on its election in October 1995 as a sign to financial markets that the new government was serious about keeping a tight hold on state spending.
